=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-ColumnSelect.md ===
# FEATURE: Column Select

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261025 V1 |
| Description | Profile only the column named by --column and reject an absent name with exit 3. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-ProfileOutput.md, FEATURE-Arguments.md, FEATURE-InputRejection.md |
| Provides    | --column behavior |
| Consumes    | profile table on standard output |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

`csvstat --column <name> <file>` writes the profile header followed by the single row for the named
column. The row is identical to the row the full profile writes for that column. A name that is not
in the header is a rejected input.

## Behavior

- Output is the header `column,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median` and exactly one
  row, for the named column, written with the same `encoding/csv` writer as the full profile.
- The name is compared to the trimmed header names as an exact string.
- A name absent from the header exits 3, writes nothing to standard output, and writes one
  diagnostic line naming the file to standard error.
- The whole file is still read and validated first, so a ragged file exits 3 regardless of the
  column named.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC column-select-matches-full-profile ===
Intent: A named column yields the profile header plus exactly the row the full profile gives that column.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
from drydock_go import cli_runner

data = "sources/employees.csv"
code, out, err = cli_runner(data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
full = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))
header = full[0]
by_name = {row[0]: row for row in full[1:]}

for name in ("salary", "id", "remote", "hire_date"):
    code, out, err = cli_runner("--column", name, data)
    assert code == 0, (name, code, out, err)
    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))
    assert len(rows) == 2, (name, rows)
    assert rows[0] == header, (name, rows[0], header)
    assert rows[1] == by_name[name], (name, rows[1], by_name[name])
=== END AC column-select-matches-full-profile ===

=== AC column-select-quoted-field ===
Intent: A column whose value contains a comma is quoted by the writer and parses back to the same row as the full profile.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
from drydock_go import cli_runner

data = "sources/employees.csv"
code, out, err = cli_runner(data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
full = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))
by_name = {row[0]: row for row in full[1:]}

name = "notes"
code, out, err = cli_runner("--column", name, data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))
assert len(rows) == 2, rows
assert rows[1] == by_name[name], (rows[1], by_name[name])
assert any("," in field for field in rows[1]), rows[1]
=== END AC column-select-quoted-field ===

=== AC column-select-absent-name ===
Intent: A column name missing from the header exits 3 and writes nothing to standard output.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

from drydock_go import cli_runner

code, out, err = cli_runner("--column", "nosuch", "sources/orders.csv")
assert code == 3, (code, out, err)
assert out == "", out
=== END AC column-select-absent-name ===

=== AC column-select-trimmed-header-name ===
Intent: The column name is matched against trimmed header names, so a padded header still resolves.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
import os
import tempfile
from drydock_go import cli_runner

name = "price"
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    path = os.path.join(tmp, "padded.csv")
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as handle:
        handle.write(f"id,  {name}  \n1,2.50\n2,3.50\n")
    code, out, err = cli_runner("--column", name, path)
    assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))
    assert len(rows) == 2, rows
    assert rows[1][0] == name, rows
=== END AC column-select-trimmed-header-name ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- The row for a named column is computed from the file, never hardcoded.
- Nothing is written to standard output when the command fails.
- Only the exact-string, trimmed header name selects a column; no prefix or case-insensitive match.

# FEATURE: Frequency

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261025 V1 |
| Description | List the most frequent non-null values of one column ordered by count descending then value ascending. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-NullValues.md, FEATURE-ProfileOutput.md, FEATURE-Arguments.md, FEATURE-InputRejection.md |
| Provides    | --freq behavior |
| Consumes    | internal/profile.IsNull |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

`csvstat --freq <name> <file>` replaces the profile with a frequency listing of one column.

## Behavior

- Output header is `value,count`, written with the `encoding/csv` writer and `\n` line endings.
- One row per distinct non-null value of the named column, values compared as exact trimmed
  strings.
- Rows are ordered by count descending, then by value ascending by byte value.
- Null values (empty, `NA`, `N/A`, `NULL` ignoring case, after trimming) are not listed.
- A column with no non-null values writes only the header and exits 0.
- At most 5 rows are written when `--top` is not given. `--top` itself is specified in
  FEATURE-FrequencyTop.md.
- A name absent from the header exits 3 with nothing on standard output.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC frequency-ordering ===
Intent: Frequencies list non-null trimmed values by count descending then byte-ordered value, matching counts computed from the input file.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
from collections import Counter
from drydock_go import cli_runner

data = "sources/orders.csv"
column = "customer"
with open(data, newline="") as handle:
    records = list(csv.reader(handle))
index = [name.strip() for name in records[0]].index(column)
nulls = {"", "na", "n/a", "null"}
values = [row[index].strip() for row in records[1:]]
counts = Counter(v for v in values if v.lower() not in nulls)
ordered = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0].encode()))
expected = [[value, str(count)] for value, count in ordered][:5]

code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", column, data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))
assert rows[0] == ["value", "count"], rows[0]
assert rows[1:] == expected, (rows[1:], expected)
=== END AC frequency-ordering ===

=== AC frequency-tie-order-by-bytes ===
Intent: Values with equal counts are ordered ascending by byte value.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
import os
import tempfile
from drydock_go import cli_runner

values = ["b", "a", "B", "c", "a", "b"]
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    path = os.path.join(tmp, "ties.csv")
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as handle:
        handle.write("v\n" + "\n".join(values) + "\n")
    code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", "v", path)
    assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))[1:]
    expected_order = sorted(set(values), key=lambda v: (-values.count(v), v.encode()))
    assert [row[0] for row in rows] == expected_order, (rows, expected_order)
    assert [int(row[1]) for row in rows] == [values.count(v) for v in expected_order], rows
=== END AC frequency-tie-order-by-bytes ===

=== AC frequency-excludes-nulls ===
Intent: Null values are not listed, and counts equal the non-null occurrences in the file.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
from collections import Counter
from drydock_go import cli_runner

data = "sources/employees.csv"
column = "manager_id"
with open(data, newline="") as handle:
    records = list(csv.reader(handle))
index = [name.strip() for name in records[0]].index(column)
nulls = {"", "na", "n/a", "null"}
values = [row[index].strip() for row in records[1:]]
counts = Counter(v for v in values if v.lower() not in nulls)

code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", column, "--top", str(len(values)), data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))[1:]
listed = {row[0]: int(row[1]) for row in rows}
assert listed == dict(counts), (listed, dict(counts))
assert not any(row[0].lower() in nulls for row in rows), rows
=== END AC frequency-excludes-nulls ===

=== AC frequency-default-limit ===
Intent: Without --top at most five rows are written, even when more distinct values exist.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
from drydock_go import cli_runner

data = "sources/employees.csv"
column = "name"
with open(data, newline="") as handle:
    records = list(csv.reader(handle))
index = [name.strip() for name in records[0]].index(column)
distinct = {row[index].strip() for row in records[1:]}
assert len(distinct) > 5

code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", column, data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))[1:]
assert len(rows) == 5, rows
=== END AC frequency-default-limit ===

=== AC frequency-all-null-column ===
Intent: A column with no non-null values writes only the header and exits 0.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
from drydock_go import cli_runner

code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", "battery", "sources/sensors.csv")
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))
assert rows == [["value", "count"]], rows
=== END AC frequency-all-null-column ===

=== AC frequency-absent-column ===
Intent: An absent column name exits 3 with nothing on standard output.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

from drydock_go import cli_runner

code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", "nosuch", "sources/orders.csv")
assert code == 3, (code, out, err)
assert out == "", out
=== END AC frequency-absent-column ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Frequencies are computed from the file examined; no value list is hardcoded.
- Values are compared as exact strings after trimming; no case folding.
- Nothing is written to standard output when the command fails.
=== END ARTIFACT ===

# FEATURE: Frequency Top

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261025 V1 |
| Description | Limit frequency rows with --top and reject a non-positive or non-integer value with exit 2. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-Frequency.md |
| Provides    | --top behavior |
| Consumes    | --freq behavior |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

`--top <n>` bounds the number of rows `--freq` writes.

## Behavior

- `--top n` writes at most `n` frequency rows; the default is 5.
- `n` must be a positive integer. Zero, a negative number, a non-numeric value, or a decimal exits
  2 with nothing on standard output.
- `--top` without `--freq` exits 2 with nothing on standard output.
- When `n` exceeds the number of distinct non-null values, all of them are listed.
- The limit applies after ordering, so the rows kept are the most frequent.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC top-limits-rows ===
Intent: --top n lists the first n rows of the full ordering, and a larger n lists every distinct value.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
from drydock_go import cli_runner

data = "sources/employees.csv"
column = "department"
with open(data, newline="") as handle:
    records = list(csv.reader(handle))
index = [name.strip() for name in records[0]].index(column)
distinct = {row[index].strip() for row in records[1:]}

code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", column, "--top", str(len(distinct) + 10), data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
full = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))[1:]
assert len(full) == len(distinct), (full, distinct)

limit = 2
code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", column, "--top", str(limit), data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))
assert rows[0] == ["value", "count"], rows[0]
assert rows[1:] == full[:limit], (rows[1:], full[:limit])
=== END AC top-limits-rows ===

=== AC top-with-column-order ===
Intent: --top may precede --freq and still limits the listing.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
from drydock_go import cli_runner

data = "sources/sensors.csv"
limit = 3
code, out, err = cli_runner("--top", str(limit), "--freq", "sensor", data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))[1:]
assert len(rows) == limit, rows
=== END AC top-with-column-order ===

=== AC top-rejects-non-positive ===
Intent: A --top value that is not a positive integer exits 2 and writes nothing to standard output.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

from drydock_go import cli_runner

data = "sources/sensors.csv"
for bad in ("0", "-1", "abc", "2.5", ""):
    code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", "sensor", "--top", bad, data)
    assert code == 2, (bad, code, out, err)
    assert out == "", (bad, out)
=== END AC top-rejects-non-positive ===

=== AC top-without-freq ===
Intent: --top without --freq exits 2 and writes nothing to standard output.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

from drydock_go import cli_runner

code, out, err = cli_runner("--top", "3", "sources/sensors.csv")
assert code == 2, (code, out, err)
assert out == "", out
=== END AC top-without-freq ===

=== AC top-missing-value ===
Intent: --top given as the last option without a value exits 2.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

from drydock_go import cli_runner

code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", "sensor", "--top")
assert code == 2, (code, out, err)
assert out == "", out
=== END AC top-missing-value ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Usage errors never write to standard output.
- The default of 5 is applied only when `--top` is absent.
=== END ARTIFACT ===
=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-TestRunner.md ===
# FEATURE: Test Runner

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261025 V1 |
| Description | Provide the POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test and exits zero only when both pass. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-FrequencyTop.md, FEATURE-ColumnSelect.md, FEATURE-ReadFailure.md, FEATURE-Build.md |
| Provides    | bin/test.sh |
| Consumes    | go vet, go test |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

`bin/test.sh` is the single command that gates every behavioral story. The project's own Go test
suite is written beside the code and covers each type, each statistic, null handling, rounding,
each output form, and each exit code, using files the tests write themselves.

## Behavior

- POSIX sh only; no bashisms. It changes to the application root (the directory above `bin/`) so it
  works from any current directory.
- It runs `go vet ./...` and then `go test ./...`, and exits zero only when both succeed. A failure
  of `go vet` stops the script with a non-zero status.
- Tests call `cli.Run(args, &stdout, &stderr)` with `bytes.Buffer` writers and write their fixture
  files under `t.TempDir()`. They never read `sources/run.sh`.
- The suite covers: each of the five types, min/max per type, sum/mean/median, half-away-from-zero
  rounding including negatives, null classification, quoting of fields with commas, frequency
  ordering and `--top`, and exit codes 1, 2, and 3.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC test-script-passes ===
Intent: bin/test.sh runs go vet and go test over the application and exits zero.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import subprocess

result = subprocess.run(["sh", "bin/test.sh"], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0, result.returncode
=== END AC test-script-passes ===

=== AC test-script-is-posix-sh ===
Intent: bin/test.sh parses under a POSIX shell without executing it.
Requires: executable=sh; scope=test

import subprocess

result = subprocess.run(["sh", "-n", "bin/test.sh"], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0, result.returncode
=== END AC test-script-is-posix-sh ===

=== AC test-script-works-from-other-directory ===
Intent: bin/test.sh succeeds when invoked from a directory other than the application root.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import os
import subprocess
import tempfile

script = os.path.abspath("bin/test.sh")
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as elsewhere:
    result = subprocess.run(["sh", script], cwd=elsewhere, capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0, result.returncode
=== END AC test-script-works-from-other-directory ===

=== AC test-suite-exists ===
Intent: The module contains automated Go tests that go test discovers and runs successfully.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import subprocess

listed = subprocess.run(["go", "test", "-list", ".", "./..."], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(listed.stdout)
print(listed.stderr)
assert listed.returncode == 0, listed.returncode
names = [line for line in listed.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith("Test")]
assert len(names) > 0, names
=== END AC test-suite-exists ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- The script uses only POSIX sh constructs and the Go toolchain; no vendored toolchain.
- Tests never read `sources/run.sh` or the supplied data files, and embed no answers from them.
=== END ARTIFACT ===
=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Conformance.md ===
# FEATURE: Conformance

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261025 V1 |
| Description | Assemble every csvstat story and pass the supplied conformance grader sh sources/run.sh. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-TestRunner.md, FEATURE-FrequencyTop.md, FEATURE-ColumnSelect.md, FEATURE-ReadFailure.md |
| Provides    | conformance with sources/run.sh |
| Consumes    | csvstat executable, bin/test.sh |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

This assembly story runs once every implementation story has closed. The supplied grader builds
`./cmd/csvstat` with `go build` and makes 22 checks of exit code and standard output against the
five supplied CSV files. The grader's exit status is the verdict.

## Behavior

- `sh sources/run.sh` is run from the application root, unfiltered, and exits zero.
- A failing check is repaired in the member stories' code. Files under `sources/` are never
  modified, rewritten, regenerated, or substituted, and application code never reads
  `sources/run.sh` or the supplied data files or embeds any answer.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC grader-passes ===
Intent: The complete csvstat passes every check of the supplied grader.
Suite: full
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import subprocess

result = subprocess.run(["sh", "sources/run.sh"], capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0, result.returncode
=== END AC grader-passes ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Do not modify, rewrite, regenerate, or substitute any file under `sources/`.
- Do not read `sources/run.sh` or any supplied data file from application code, and do not
  hardcode a statistic, a type, or a value list.
- The grader is run unfiltered; no check is skipped or reinterpreted.
=== END ARTIFACT ===

Intent: Frequencies list non-null trimmed values by count descending then byte-ordered value, matching counts computed from the input file.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
from collections import Counter
from drydock_go import cli_runner

data = "sources/orders.csv"
column = "customer"
with open(data, newline="") as handle:
    records = list(csv.reader(handle))
index = [name.strip() for name in records[0]].index(column)
nulls = {"", "na", "n/a", "null"}
values = [row[index].strip() for row in records[1:]]
counts = Counter(v for v in values if v.lower() not in nulls)
ordered = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0].encode()))
expected = [[value, str(count)] for value, count in ordered][:5]

code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", column, data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))
assert rows[0] == ["value", "count"], rows[0]
assert rows[1:] == expected, (rows[1:], expected)
=== END AC frequency-ordering ===

=== AC frequency-tie-order-by-bytes ===
Intent: Values with equal counts are ordered ascending by byte value.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
import os
import tempfile
from drydock_go import cli_runner

values = ["b", "a", "B", "c", "a", "b"]
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    path = os.path.join(tmp, "ties.csv")
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as handle:
        handle.write("v\n" + "\n".join(values) + "\n")
    code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", "v", path)
    assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))[1:]
    expected_order = sorted(set(values), key=lambda v: (-values.count(v), v.encode()))
    assert [row[0] for row in rows] == expected_order, (rows, expected_order)
    assert [int(row[1]) for row in rows] == [values.count(v) for v in expected_order], rows
=== END AC frequency-tie-order-by-bytes ===

# FEATURE: Frequency Top

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261025 V1 |
| Description | Limit frequency rows with --top and reject a non-positive or non-integer value with exit 2. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-Frequency.md |
| Provides    | --top behavior |
| Consumes    | --freq behavior |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

`--top <n>` bounds the number of rows `--freq` writes.

## Behavior

- `--top n` writes at most `n` frequency rows; the default is 5.
- `n` must be a positive integer. Zero, a negative number, a non-numeric value, or a decimal exits
  2 with nothing on standard output.
- `--top` without `--freq` exits 2 with nothing on standard output.
- When `n` exceeds the number of distinct non-null values, all of them are listed.
- The limit applies after ordering, so the rows kept are the most frequent.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC top-limits-rows ===
Intent: --top n lists the first n rows of the full ordering, and a larger n lists every distinct value.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import csv
import io
from drydock_go import cli_runner

data = "sources/employees.csv"
column = "department"
with open(data, newline="") as handle:
    records = list(csv.reader(handle))
index = [name.strip() for name in records[0]].index(column)
distinct = {row[index].strip() for row in records[1:]}

code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", column, "--top", str(len(distinct) + 10), data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
full = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))[1:]
assert len(full) == len(distinct), (full, distinct)

limit = 2
code, out, err = cli_runner("--freq", column, "--top", str(limit), data)
assert code == 0, (code, out, err)
rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))
assert rows[0] == ["value", "count"], rows[0]
assert rows[1:] == full[:limit], (rows[1:], full[:limit])

# FEATURE: Test Runner

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261025 V1 |
| Description | Provide the POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test and exits zero only when both pass. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-FrequencyTop.md, FEATURE-ColumnSelect.md, FEATURE-ReadFailure.md, FEATURE-Build.md |
| Provides    | bin/test.sh |
| Consumes    | go vet, go test |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

`bin/test.sh` is the single command that gates every behavioral story. The project's own Go test
suite is written beside the code and covers each type, each statistic, null handling, rounding,
each output form, and each exit code, using files the tests write themselves.

## Behavior

- POSIX sh only; no bashisms. It changes to the application root (the directory above `bin/`) so it
  works from any current directory.
- It runs `go vet ./...` and then `go test ./...`, and exits zero only when both succeed. A failure
  of `go vet` stops the script with a non-zero status.
- Tests call `cli.Run(args, &stdout, &stderr)` with `bytes.Buffer` writers and write their fixture
  files under `t.TempDir()`. They never read `sources/run.sh`.
- The suite covers: each of the five types, min/max per type, sum/mean/median, half-away-from-zero
  rounding including negatives, null classification, quoting of fields with commas, frequency
  ordering and `--top`, and exit codes 1, 2, and 3.

## Purpose

This assembly story runs once every implementation story has closed. The supplied grader builds
`./cmd/csvstat` with `go build` and makes 22 checks of exit code and standard output against the
five supplied CSV files. The grader's exit status is the verdict.

## Behavior

- `sh sources/run.sh` is run from the application root, unfiltered, and exits zero.
- A failing check is repaired in the member stories' code. Files under `sources/` are never
  modified, rewritten, regenerated, or substituted, and application code never reads
  `sources/run.sh` or the supplied data files or embeds any answer.
